requirements.title: Enum enumerators share the kind interoperable with the corresponding C enum
requirements.source: 7.6.1, p1, p2; J3/24-007, 18 December 2023, physical PDF 109.
requirements.definition: All INTEGER enumerators in one enum-def have one kind. That kind is interoperable with the hypothetical C2018 enumerated type whose enumeration constants have the same specified values in the same declaration order. The rule applies with or without an optional named enum type; it does not select C_INT or a fixed width.

Use the actual enum-derived carrier kind or named enum type, never assumed C_INT equality.

requirements.oracle:
A bounded same-definition KIND/value witness and separately qualified C interoperability witness have distinct evidentiary roles. C_INT is available for the cited evaluation route, not a prescribed enum kind. A complete C companion proof is not a compiler consensus experiment.

Finite unnamed-enum implementation: 1 shared runtime program represents 1 selected facets. Independent literal vectors are checked separately for each definition, including flat/split forms, negative/repeated values and fresh-definition reset where applicable. Every definition compares each INTEGER enumerator's KIND to its own first member; no cross-definition or numeric KIND-code equality is imposed. Small value-only INT conversions use the required default INTEGER representation. All other original plans remain pending; observations do not confer source/case approval.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Use defined values and source-derived finite expectations, not compiler agreement. Keep enum type, its INTEGER enumerators and ENUMERATION TYPE distinct. KIND identifiers, byte width, C_INT equality, a minimum representation, unsigned wrap, padding bits and additional supported kinds are not assumed. Runtime effects remain runtime on implementation failure. No companion profile or C experiment is supplied in this bounded runtime packet.

requirements.title: Named enum values correspond to the enumerator integer kind and constructors produce those values
requirements.definition: The value set of a named enum type corresponds one-to-one with all possible values of its enumerators' INTEGER kind, not only the listed enumerator values. Each enum value has the same internal representation as its corresponding integer. An enum constructor produces a scalar of the specified enum type with the specified internal representation; its operand must separately meet C7113 and p7's range condition.

The sequence is over the whole enum-def, not restarted by each ENUMERATOR statement.

This plain prose value restriction does not itself mandate a diagnostic.

KIND identifiers, byte width, C_INT equality, a minimum representation, unsigned wrap, padding bits and additional supported kinds are not assumed. Future runtime effects must remain runtime on implementation failure. Extreme unsigned carriers, wider kinds, BOZ padding/sign interpretation and any desired diagnostic policy remain separate explicit gates.

accounting.rationale: Original NOTE1, PDF110: conditional unsigned/signed representation explanation, not a new local arithmetic or diagnostic policy.
The example condition is a companion using an unsigned C type for its enum representation, not a promise that every companion does so.
The note explains use of the signed Fortran integer type of the corresponding width; it does not prescribe a width or KIND number.
Some C enumerator values may not be representable in that signed integer type. Do not infer equal signed/unsigned mathematical domains or a wraparound result.
Type interoperability remains distinct from representability of every C value. Extreme unsigned-value candidates require separate source/companion qualification.
Original NOTE2, PDF110: a C2018-based evaluation explanation; no hard-coded kind equality or new implementation algorithm is required.
The note cites the C2018 requirement that enumeration constants fit C int.
C_INT can be used to evaluate these values before selecting the enum's representation.
The evaluation route does not say the resulting enumerator KIND is C_INT, default INTEGER, or a minimum SELECTED_INT_KIND result.
Original NOTE3, PDF110 elaborates p5. Its representation condition must not be replaced by a type-identity or name-matching claim.
The cited C compatibility condition includes names as well as values and order.
The Fortran companion condition instead requires the same representation for identical ordered value lists even when names differ.
Neither matching representation nor ignored names for that representation condition erases C compatibility or Fortran enum-type identity distinctions.
Original NOTE4, PDF110 preserves the example's values, processor dependence, conditional equivalence and valid KIND inquiry target.
The illustrated explicit values4/9 and following implicit10 exemplify p6.
The example kind is processor dependent, not an intrinsic numeric KIND code.
The selected representation must suffice for the example's4/9/10; this is not a guarantee for unrelated larger literals.
The SELECTED_INT_KIND(2) declaration is only a possible equivalent, not a required equality or prescribed selection algorithm.
KIND(RED) identifies the INTEGER enumerator's actual kind for another INTEGER declaration; KIND(enum-type-object) is not authorized.
Original NOTE5, PDF111 explains p6 across statements; do not invent a reset at each ENUMERATOR statement.
One versus several ENUMERATOR statements does not change the definition's effect when enumerator order is unchanged.
Declaration order, not statement count, controls p6's immediately preceding enumerator.
Original NOTE6, PDF111 is fully retained as qualified examples and canonical consumer relationships, not additional local mandatory executions.
The example defines two named enum types; their integer enumerators do not collapse the two type definitions.
The illustrated BIND(C)/VALUE interface and enum output require18.3 and the canonical I/O rules, not a local enum-type-as-INTEGER identity.

An INTEGER expression with a primary from the correct enum can initialize that enum type under7.3.3/8.2/10.2.1.2. This is broader than requiring a bare enumerator and narrower than accepting every INTEGER expression.

myenum(12345) is a valid illustration only on a representation that can hold12345. The definition's1/2/3 does not itself establish that range; retain ENS-Q01 rather than copy an unconditional success case.
The negative bound is -HUGE(one), with one an INTEGER enumerator. It is not HUGE of an enum-type object or an assumption that signed values have the same mathematical meaning in a C unsigned carrier.

The invalid raw-integer initializer/call examples lack the necessary enum primary. Their large literals may add a range defect; a future isolated compatibility candidate must instead use a known-representable raw value.
The other enum's f1 remains an INTEGER constant; the issue is wrong defining-enum provenance in the expression, not a claim that f1 has TYPE(flags).
Original PDF109: the separate fine units preserve every condition and distinguish definitions, effects, restrictions and examples.
An interoperable enumeration denotes a set of interoperable enumerators.
A named enum type is optional; an unnamed ENUM,BIND(C) definition does not create a nameable enum type.
The complete enum-def, not just its header, defines that interoperable enumeration.
An interoperable enumerator is a named INTEGER constant, not a value whose declared type is the optional enum type.
A named enum type belongs to the nonintrinsic category.
An enum type is not a derived type. Derived-type-only rules cannot be imported by analogy.
The enum type itself has no type parameter; the INTEGER kind of its enumerators is a different notion.

The optional enum-type-name controls whether this definition also defines a named enum type.
When present, that name identifies the enum type defined by this enum-def; no nameable type is inferred for an unnamed block.
The named enum type is interoperable.18.3.3 supplies the corresponding C enum and C integer-type interoperability relationships.
The paragraph defines the type-specifier and same-definition relationship; it is not an executable classification requirement.
An enum type specifier identifies its type; the original 'specifiers' typography does not introduce an extra operation.
Reference to the same enum type definition is the stated same-type criterion. Matching integer values, KIND numbers or companion representations are not that defining reference.
